items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. Author: Lisa Doumbouya   Research programme: Harmonic Physics Research Programme keywords: String theory; Sine-Gordon equation; Pohlmeyer reduction; Classical strings; Phase dynamics; Coupled phase fields; Relative phase; Cosine interaction; Breather solutions; Solitons; Nonlinear dynamics; Expansion and contraction; Computational reproducibility; Phase theory; Harmonic Physics
items.title: String Theory and Phase Dynamics: An Exact Conditional Sine-Gordon Correspondence

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.
items.title: Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc

items.summary: Version 1.6 adds four preregistered analyses of LEGA-C star-forming discs at z ~ 0.8 and of SPARC: KCAL, a calibration of the gas pressure coefficient against stellar JAM masses; PIPE-6, a0 at R_e and 2R_e from ionized gas; PIPE-7, a local SPARC control; and PIPE-8, JAM-gas offsets and a0 at both radii. It also adds two analyses that were designed but not run (PIPE-5, GAP). Combined reading: in the same galaxies the gas a0 rises outward (+0.30 dex on 40), the JAM a0 does not (−0.08, no pre-stated reading), and the JAM-gas mass offset falls outward (−0.16). With measured mass models local discs show no rise; with the LEGA-C stellar recipe the 53 massive discs show none, but all 138 rise by +0.14. Preregistrations and code were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) and audited by fresh Claude sessions; locks are self-recorded SHA-256 manifests with UTC times. See README_v1.6.md for contents, provenance, hashes and every post-score edit.   Version 1.5 adds a synthesis note, "What the a0(z) tests say together: a falling g_obs/g_bar where the errors allow a test, and a fitted scale set by the baryonic and pressure inputs at R_e" (a0z_synthesis_note.pdf; scripts, outputs, figures, searches and audits in a0z_v1.5_SYNTHESIS.zip). It is exploratory and post hoc: it was designed after every result in the record was known, it is not preregistered, and it changes no scored label. It uses the record's frozen PIPE-2 and PIPE-3 code unchanged as a library. What it finds: - Shape. LEGA-C (147 galaxies), the one sample whose errors allow a shape test, prefers a ratio g_obs/g_bar that falls with g_bar (PIPE-3's R; classical margin 12, about one jackknife standard error above the threshold of 4) across gas multipliers 0-2, pressure multipliers 0.5-2 and stellar shifts -0.2 to +0.1 dex. MSA-3D's flat trend (18 galaxies) does not reappear. - Scale. No sample measures a0. At LEGA-C's accelerations the fitted a0 responds about three times as fast as the baryonic mass at R_e: locally d ln a0/d ln M* = -2.2, d ln a0/d ln M_gas = -0.6, d ln a0/d ln k_press = +0.8, explained by the interpolation function's leverage (L = 2.96). Shifts of +/-0.1 dex in stellar mass span a0 = 0.78-2.25. A universal a0 = 1.2 and an evolving a0 = 2.2 differ by about 0.13 dex in stellar mass, or a factor of four in inner gas. Every record value except MSA-3D's lies inside the ranges these inputs produce. - Matched in stellar mass, LEGA-C, KROSS and RC100 have median offsets from one RAR that are not distinguishable, although direct fits in the window differ. No dependence of a0 on stellar mass is detected inside any sample. - Reading: the record does not require an evolving a0; a0 at z ~ 1 cannot be read off until the baryonic mass at R_e is known to a few hundredths of a dex. - Can it be tested now? Searches (identifiers and counts only) found almost no CO or dust detections in the high-a0 samples (MSA-3D 0 of 23; MUSE-DARK 6 of its 126-galaxy parent). For the nine RC100 galaxies with PHIBSS CO, a preregistered test would decide with probability 0.07-0.13 (PIPE4_FEASIBILITY.md), so no test was run. Audits: three independent fresh-session audits. Round 1: 1 BLOCKER (the draft attributed the scale to cold gas; the stellar masses are the stronger lever), 7 MAJOR; round 2: 1 MAJOR (Table I's SPARC row); round 3: 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 3 MINOR, all fixed. Every script and figure was reproduced byte for byte in each round. Findings and change logs are in synthesis/audit_r1-r3/. Files added in v1.5: a0z_synthesis_note.pdf (SHA-256 7b4493a02a8e857aa1f415f923b82fa088adf5b1df92b2b51febd1c4b9942606) and a0z_v1.5_SYNTHESIS.zip (SHA-256 be552c3bc715090559ef4e68500e5d5b8aabbdfb6243954b387d0a0b5f97f72f). Input catalogues are those already in v1.0 (RC100), v1.3 (KROSS) and v1.4 (LEGA-C). This computes the thermometer, not the engine; the inertia coupling remains unsolved.   Version 1.4 adds PIPE-3 (scored 13 October 2026; folder pipe3/ inside a0z_v1.4_PIPE3.zip). PIPE-3 is a pr

items.summary: Description This dataset accompanies a comparative evolutionary-genomics study of ancestral cytosine substitution patterns across human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla lineages. Using hg38-centered UCSC multiz primate alignments and a seven-species phylogenetic framework, we reconstructed ancestral nucleotide states and quantified cytosine substitutions across all 22 human autosomes. The analysis examined CG, CHG and CHH sequence contexts, 256 strand-canonicalized ancestral 5-mer motifs, and lineage-specific substitution patterns. The deposited files include: Chromosome-level ancestral-site datasets at a minimum ancestral-state posterior probability of 0.95. Chromosome-specific 5-mer substitution summaries and quality-control records. Genome-wide cytosine substitution frequencies and context-enrichment ratios. Chromosome-bootstrap uncertainty estimates and cross-lineage motif comparisons. Statistical analyses of lineage-specific motif deviations, including simultaneous confidence intervals. Leave-one-autosome-out predictive comparisons of ancestral 3-mer and 5-mer sequence context. Frozen methodology documentation, validation records, checksums and the fixed seven-species phylogenetic tree. The dataset supports independent examination and downstream reanalysis of the reported numerical findings. Data provenance: UCSC Genome Browser hg38-centered 30-primate multiz alignments, restricted to seven primate species. Computational methods: IQ-TREE 2.3.6 ancestral-state reconstruction under GTR+F+G4, followed by custom Python-based sequence-context and statistical analyses. Limitations: The archive contains processed ancestral-site data and numerical outputs, not the original complete multiple-sequence alignments. It does not contain ancestral DNA methylation measurements, direct estimates of net CpG gain or loss, or calibrated mutation rates. Associated code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23425960 Archive organization: This dataset is distributed across two Zenodo records. This record contains Part 1 of 2. Part 2 is available at https://zenodo.org/records/23442145 . Both parts are required to reconstruct the complete archive. Download all files from both records and follow the instructions in RECONSTRUCTION.txt to assemble and verify the dataset.
items.title: Ancestral Cytosine Sequence-Context Substitution Data Across Four Hominid Lineages: A 22-Autosome Comparative Analysis. Part 1

items.summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies Marco Mantovanelli's A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws. It contains the manuscript PDF, complete LaTeX source, six vector figures, independent verification programs, figure-generation code, numerical reports, and sampled figure data. The paper studies Q(n) = Q(n - Q(n-1)) + Q(n - Q(n-2)) - (-1)^n for n >= 8, with the seven prescribed initial values (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5). A causal binary-word construction proves global existence and an exact factorization into three signed excursions. Their uniformly convergent Gaussian profiles explain three limiting sign transitions per standard dyadic block and a sharp normalized error envelope of approximately 0.067088003576. The paper also proves exact finite transition locations, an ordered frequency factorization, a shifted 2-adic valuation law on pure dyadic value blocks, and a summatory asymptotic with an explicit continuous periodic term. The archived verification compares all 33,554,432 directly computed terms with an independent word reconstruction, checks complete frequency blocks through level 21, and verifies the exact summatory identity at every even cutoff from 8 through 33,554,432. Separate programs audit the word maps, finite transitions, and exact two-head identities. These computations supplement the general proofs in the manuscript. The original perturbation, OEIS A394051, is discussed for comparison.
items.title: A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws (Reproducibility Archive)

items.summary: Code, trained weights and campaign results for the paper "Morphological diffusion by ball births: generative models of binary images with exact Betti increments" by M. Zéraï, submitted to the Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision. The model generates binary images by births of maximal balls. Its forward process is a random granulometry, and its reverse process learns a birth map. morpho_repro.tar.gz contains the implementation (model, sampler, exact Euler increments, measurement protocol), the averaged (EMA) weights of all trained models on the three datasets (GRF, BBBC039 nuclei masks, MNIST), the campaign reports and logs, and the GRF data. README.md gives the hyperparameters, the source of each table and the reproduction commands. figs_print.tar.gz contains the figure boards of the paper with their statistics. The BBBC039 masks and MNIST are public and are downloaded by prepare_data.sh. Note: the two archives are gzip-compressed tar files, deposited as morpho_repro.tar and figs_print.tar (README.md names them morpho_repro.tar.gz and figs_print.tar.gz). Extract them with: tar xzf morpho_repro.tar
items.title: Morphological diffusion by ball births: code, trained weights and campaign results

items.summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
items.title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

items.summary: This archive contains supplementary code, data, finite certificates, and reproduction instructions for “Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces” by Makoto Ozawa (arXiv:2605.25322). This release accompanies the 41-page revision prepared in October 2026 and preserves all files from the two supplementary archives published in the previous Zenodo version. The computations concern embedded polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves. Polygons are identified under translations, proper cubic rotations, cyclic changes of starting point, and reversal of traversal; spatial reflections are retained. The archive includes the original implementations, seed files, search summaries, and explicit merge-path certificates, together with the complete minimal-layer material for the figure-eight knot and the knot 6_3. For the figure-eight knot, four minimal-layer components at length 30 merge into one component at cap 32. For 6_3, twelve minimal-layer components at length 40 merge into two mirror-related branches at cap 42 and one branch at cap 44. These statements concern the branches originating in the minimal layers, rather than an enumeration of every component at higher caps. The new trefoil supplement certifies six nonminimal components born at length 26 for a fixed chirality. Five first meet the minimal layer at cap 28, whereas a 20-state component first meets it at cap 30. The archive supplies closed component lists, capped-component separation certificates, explicit connecting paths, verification programs, and audit logs. The individual component and exact merge-height certificates do not assume exhaustion of the length-26 population; exhaustiveness at that level remains conditional on the reported literature population. The trefoil material also includes the actual BFACF path used in Figure 2: 47 configurations connected by 46 moves, with maximum length 30. All coordinates, the complete sequence of configurations, figure-generation code, and independent transition checks are provided. Additional checks verify coordinate spans of the specified trefoil components and singleton capped components for supplied 48-edge representatives of 8_3 and 8_7, including an improper spatial symmetry of the 8_3 representative. The release includes the corresponding manuscript source and figures, current documentation, checksums, provenance records, and a verification runner. Historical manuscripts are retained separately in the legacy directory; the current manuscript source is arxiv_revision/main.tex. The documentation distinguishes certified finite results from conditional completeness statements and open questions concerning eventual connectivity, Gordian configurations, and unbounded strong local-minimum birth levels. Requirements: Python 3 for the verification scripts and a C++17 compiler for the large capped-component audits. Regenerating the trefoil figures additionally requires NumPy and Matplotlib. Detailed commands and the scope of each verification are given in the included README files.
items.title: Supplementary code and data for "Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces"

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-three entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: Replication files for “Bans versus Controlled Access: Reserve Substitution and Issuer Buybacks under Financial Sanctions”. The A7A5 archive covers the TRON base contract TLeVfrdym8RoJreJ23dAGyfJDygRtiWKBZ from 7–27 August 2025 UTC. Data were retrieved on 17 October 2026 UTC. It includes 5,244 unique events from 37 daily response pages, additional event-class and receipt checks, frozen source responses and request provenance, event-level records, daily and weekly aggregates, supply accounting, data definitions, and analysis and verification scripts. Coverage is specific to the queried contract and provider. Gross transfers do not measure trading volume, beneficial ownership, reserve flows, or issuer buyback expenditure. The pilot is descriptive and does not identify a causal sanctions effect. The model archive contains Python scripts and supplied outputs for hypothetical numerical examples of route substitution, constrained issuer purchases, monitoring-dependent depth, surplus access and fallback. Parameters are not calibrated to A7A5. Both archives use Python 3.9 or later and its standard library; their README files give offline reproduction commands. Access: metadata are public; files are restricted and available on request to the corresponding author, hyoungkang@hanyang.ac.kr. The accompanying RIGHTS_AND_SOURCES.md distinguishes author-created materials from third-party responses. Rights in original materials are reserved; no blanket open license is granted for the mixed archive. The associated manuscript is unpublished.
items.title: A7A5 pilot data and model replication files for Bans versus Controlled Access

items.summary: rnaseq-flow offline Singularity container bundle (v1.7.0) A complete set of Singularity/Apptainer container images for running the rnaseq-flow bulk RNA-seq pipeline on systems with no internet access — Trusted Research Environments, secure enclaves, and air-gapped HPC. Built for pipeline release 1.7.0. By default rnaseq-flow provisions several containers on the fly with Nextflow Wave, which contacts an external service at run time. That is not possible in an air-gapped setting. This bundle pre-materialises every image the pipeline can use, so a run resolves all 26 containers from local disk and makes no outbound connection. Contents 26 Singularity images (~7 GB). Twenty are pass-through copies of the upstream Bioconda/BioContainers images: STAR, HISAT2, Salmon, kallisto, fastp, FastQC, MultiQC, RSeQC, subread/featureCounts, samtools, deepTools, rMATS, STAR-Fusion, tximport, edgeR, IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR, genomepy and Python. Seven are built from the pipeline's Conda specifications: DESeq2 with apeglm and pheatmap, edgeR with tximport, DEXSeq with tximport, fgsea, gprofiler2, msigdbr, and the Quarto reporting environment. nf-prov — plugin for part of rendering provenance reports for pipeline runs tre.config — a Nextflow profile that disables Wave and pins the seven Conda-built processes to the image names in this bundle. README.txt — usage summary. Usage tar -xf rnaseq-flow-1.7.0-singularity.tar export NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$PWD/singularity-1.7.0 nextflow run main.nf -c $NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR/tre.config -profile tre,<your-executor-profile> --input samplesheet.csv --aligner star ... Verify the download with: sha256sum -c rnaseq-flow-1.7.0-singularity.tar.sha256 Notes The tre profile requires this bundle. The seven Conda-built images are named locally to it and resolve nowhere online, so the profile is not usable on its own. Licensing. Each image carries the licences of its own upstream software. This record redistributes them unmodified for offline use and does not relicense them. Source: https://github.com/nicholas-owen/rnaseq-flow
items.title: rnaseq-flow offline Singularity container bundle (v1.7.0)

items.summary: Singing Accompaniment Generation (SAG) is the process of generating instrumental music for a given clean vocal input. However, existing SAG techniques use source-separated vocals as input and overfit to separation artifacts. This creates a critical train-test mismatch, leading to failure on clean, real-world vocal inputs. We introduce AnyAccomp, a framework that resolves this by decoupling accompaniment generation from source-dependent artifacts. AnyAccomp first employs a quantized melodic bottleneck, using a chromagram and a VQ-VAE to extract a discrete and timbre-invariant representation of the core melody. A subsequent flow-matching model then generates the accompaniment conditioned on these robust codes. Experiments show AnyAccomp achieves competitive performance on separated-vocal benchmarks while significantly outperforming baselines on generalization test sets of clean studio vocals and, notably, solo instrumental tracks. This demonstrates a qualitative leap in generalization, enabling robust accompaniment for instruments - a task where existing models completely fail - and paving the way for more versatile music co-creation tools. Demo audio and code: https://anyaccomp.github.io
items.title: AnyAccomp: Generalizable Accompaniment Generation via Quantized Melodic Bottleneck

items.summary: C. J Tully. Independent Research https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   18 th October 2026                   Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late. Something happens. A sound, a face, a tightness in the chest. Before you have chosen anything, a voice — yours, apparently — has already named it, judged it, and filed it under a chapter called me. You do not notice the filing. You notice the file. And so you spend your days inside a commentary about a world you have not, strictly speaking, met. This is not a moral failure. It is a timing error. Awareness is not a mood you work up and not a belief you adopt. It is what is already underway before the sentence starts. The breath you are taking does not consult your biography. The light on the wall does not ask what you meant to become. For a fraction of a second there is contact without a commentator. Then the commentator returns, a little late, a little proud, and explains what just occurred as if the explanation were the event. People talk about waking up as if it were a prize for the patient and the pure. It is closer to catching a clerical mistake. You have been treating the report as the room. The report is useful. It gets you across streets, through grief, into love, out of traffic. It is also not the thing it reports on. The word water has never once made a hand wet. Watch the exact moment a thought claims you. There is a sensation, then a grab. The grab feels like identity. It is older than that, and thinner. It is a habit of ownership so practiced it forgot it was optional. You do not have to defeat it. You only have to notice that noticing is already happening, and that the one who seems to be doing the noticing cannot be found as an object inside what is noticed. Sit with that past the point of comfort. Comfort is how the narration gets rehired. If the “you” who plans, defends, remembers, and suffers is a pattern appearing in awareness, then who has been afraid all this time? Not a cosmic answer. A local one. Look. Fear is weather. The sky it crosses was not manufactured by the storm. Nothing theatrical follows from this. You will still want things. You will still lose them. You will still answer the message and miss the person. The only change is a small, stubborn order of operations: experience first, story second. And the recognition, quiet enough to miss if you perform it, that you were never inside the story. You were the place it was being told. That place does not improve. It does not arrive. It does not need you to become someone else in order to be what it already is. The only work, if it can even be called work, is to stop leaving a half-second early — to remain, once, with what is here before you agree with your own explanation of it. Stay. The explanation can wait. It always could.
items.title: Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late.

items.summary: MULTI-AGENT ROUTING OF NEUROVASCULAR MICROROBOT SWARMS AT THE LIMIT This research monograph develops a falsifiable, non-clinical framework for routing heterogeneous microrobotic teams through branching neurovascular vessel phantoms. It asks whether decentralized task assignment, flow-aware navigation, independently tracked agent identity, and verifiable recovery can improve qualified sensing or inert-sample collection without increasing collision, occlusion, flow disturbance, thermal burden, sample confusion, or residual material risk. Organized around low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics, multi-agent coordination, and independently enforced physical safety boundaries, the volume contains 30 mathematical derivation plates, 82 full research chapters with five separately paginated sections each, 200 detailed Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger distinguishes established component physics and published demonstrations from the original system-level hypotheses proposed here. Strong passive-transport, single-agent, and information-matched centralized alternatives remain valid competitors throughout. Research failures, abandoned models, experimental uncertainty, and successor reconstruction are treated as scientific outputs, not editorial defects. The monograph provides a research architecture and prospective tests, not results from experiments performed for this publication. It does not assert demonstrated autonomous navigation in human cerebral vessels, clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy, or authorization for human intervention.
items.title: MULTI-AGENT ROUTING OF NEUROVASCULAR MICROROBOT SWARMS AT THE LIMIT This research monograph develops a falsifiable, non-clinical framework for routing heterogeneous microrobotic teams through branching neurovascular vessel phantoms. items.summary: Audio deepfakes generated by neural text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems threaten speaker verification and public discourse at scale. The core challenge is cross-dataset generalization: detectors trained on one synthesis pipeline collapse on unseen forgeries. We argue that this failure is primarily because of structural synthetic speech artifacts which are multi-timescale trajectory anomalies. Though every existing detector aggregates a fixed-window frame statistics, this misaligns the architecture with the signal. We propose FlowFake, a Liquid Time-Constant (LTC) architecture whose hidden state evolves via a learned ODE, with per-neuron adaptive time constants simultaneously resolving spectral (10ms) and prosodic (2s) cues. At only 34K parameters FlowFake achieves formal BIBO stability and O(dt^4) integration error. On a four-dataset cross domain benchmark (ASVspoof2019-LA, FakeOrReal, InTheWild, MLAAD), FlowFake reaches 75.29% on ASVspoof2019 trained only on FakeOrReal and 79.97% trained only on MLAAD. It outperforms RawGAT-ST and Whisper-DF on every evaluated pair and matching SSL Wav2vec2 (300x larger) at 0.01% of its parameter count. The source code is available on : https://github.com/GhostRider2023/FlowFake
items.title: FlowFake: Liquid Networks for Audio Deepfake Detection

items.summary: In speech enhancement and source separation, signal-to-noise ratio is a ubiquitous objective measure of denoising/separation quality. A decade ago, the BSS_eval toolkit was developed to give researchers worldwide a way to evaluate the quality of their algorithms in a simple, fair, and hopefully insightful way: it attempted to account for channel variations, and to not only evaluate the total distortion in the estimated signal but also split it in terms of various factors such as remaining interference, newly added artifacts, and channel errors. In recent years, hundreds of papers have been relying on this toolkit to evaluate their proposed methods and compare them to previous works, often arguing that differences on the order of 0.1 dB proved the effectiveness of a method over others. We argue here that the signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) implemented in the BSS_eval toolkit has generally been improperly used and abused, especially in the case of single-channel separation, resulting in misleading results. We propose to use a slightly modified definition, resulting in a simpler, more robust measure, called scale-invariant SDR (SI-SDR). We present various examples of critical failure of the original SDR that SI-SDR overcomes.
items.title: SDR - half-baked or well done?

items.summary: The spoof speech detection (SSD) is the essential countermeasure for automatic speaker verification systems. Although SSD with magnitude features in the frequency domain has shown promising results, the phase information also can be important to capture the artefacts of certain types of spoofing attacks. Thus, both magnitude and phase features must be considered to ensure the generalization ability to diverse types of spoofing attacks. In this paper, we investigate the failure reason of feature-level fusion of the previous works through the entropy analysis from which we found that the randomness difference between magnitude and phase features is large, which can interrupt the feature-level fusion via backend neural network; thus, we propose a phase network to reduce that difference. Our SSD system: phase network equipped Res2Net achieved significant performance improvement, specifically in the spoofing attack for which the phase information is considered to be important. Also, we demonstrate our SSD system in both known- and unknown-kind SSD scenarios for practical applications.
items.title: Phase-Aware Spoof Speech Detection Based on Res2Net with Phase Network

items.summary: Coding agents can now interpret a specification, implement it, write and execute tests, repair failures, and declare the result ready for release. When the same agentic system produces both the software and the evidence of its correctness, a passing test suite no longer constitutes independent evidence. Visible tests become an optimization target, and code, tests, and oracles may share a single misinterpretation of the specification. This paper argues that agent-produced software requires an assurance plane that is structurally independent of the build plane. We first characterize four gaps along the chain from stakeholder intent to production, namely the requirement, conformance, evaluation, and model gaps, and identify which of them verification can close. We then propose a framework that separates building from verifying, introduces a Verification Contract stating what must be demonstrated before release, and organizes verification in two phases: a specification-first phase designed without access to the implementation, and an implementation-aware phase that strengthens the evidence through mutation analysis, property-based testing, and fuzzing. The resulting evidence is consolidated into an assurance report that makes residual uncertainty explicit and leaves the release decision to a human. We evaluate the framework in a pre-registered study on three stateful services, two of them written by third-party models, and an EvalPlus pilot, comparing self-validation with independent verification under context-level and model-level independence. The builder's programs were correct, but its own tests missed subtle interactions: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006), and surfaced the ambiguities of the specification, at the price of rare false oracles. A verifier from another provider did not add detection. The framework and the study provide a basis for governing the release of software produced by agents.
items.title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software

items.summary: Climate change affects human well-being through interacting physical, ecological, infrastructural, and socioeconomic processes rather than through a single exposure or disease pathway. Major assessments identify observed harms to health, food and water security, livelihoods, settlements, and ecosystems, alongside increasing risks with additional warming (IPCC, 2022a). This narrative review develops a cross-sector framework from a source inventory of 154 human-impact pathways in 14 domains, supported by major assessments, selected peer-reviewed studies, and institutional datasets. Literature selection used targeted web-index searches and source verification through 2 October 2026; the review does not estimate pooled effects or claim exhaustive systematic coverage. The synthesis distinguishes direct injury and illness, ecosystem-mediated harms, failures of essential services, financial transmission, and losses of social and cultural continuity. Representative quantitative findings illustrate substantial existing burdens, but attribution studies, ecological associations, exposure models, displacement records, and conditional forecasts measure different quantities and cannot be combined into a universal five-year trajectory (Vicedo-Cabrera et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2026; Clement et al., 2021). Compound hazards and service interdependencies can increase losses beyond the directly affected sector, while repeated shocks can reduce the capacity to recover or adapt (Zscheischler et al., 2018; IPCC, 2023). A reporting framework is proposed that records the outcome, population, baseline, geography, time horizon, emissions and development assumptions, adaptation, and uncertainty for each indicator. The central contribution is an integrated interpretation and measurement architecture, not a new forecast of global mortality, migration, or societal collapse. Effective assessment should preserve evidence of serious and interacting harms without converting uncertain thresholds or heterogeneous studies into unsupported calendar-specific predictions.
items.title: Climate change impacts humans: A cross-sector narrative review of impact pathways, cascading risks, and accountable quantification

items.summary: We propose DeepASA, a multi-purpose model for auditory scene analysis that performs multi-input multi-output (MIMO) source separation, dereverberation, sound event detection (SED), audio classification, and direction-of-arrival estimation (DoAE) within a unified framework. DeepASA is designed for complex auditory scenes where multiple, often similar, sound sources overlap in time and move dynamically in space. To achieve robust and consistent inference across tasks, we introduce an object-oriented processing (OOP) strategy. This approach encapsulates diverse auditory features into object-centric representations and refines them through a chain-of-inference (CoI) mechanism. The pipeline comprises a dynamic temporal kernel-based feature extractor, a transformer-based aggregator, and an object separator that yields per-object features. These features feed into multiple task-specific decoders. Our object-centric representations naturally resolve the parameter association ambiguity inherent in traditional track-wise processing. However, early-stage object separation can lead to failure in downstream ASA tasks. To address this, we implement temporal coherence matching (TCM) within the chain-of-inference, enabling multi-task fusion and iterative refinement of object features using estimated auditory parameters. We evaluate DeepASA on representative spatial audio benchmark datasets, including ASA2, MC-FUSS, and STARSS23. Experimental results show that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in both source separation and auditory parameter estimation under diverse spatial auditory scenes.
items.title: DeepASA: An Object-Oriented Multi-Purpose Network for Auditory Scene Analysis

items.summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
items.title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

items.summary: DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY is a long-form philosophical poem exploring the courage of individuals who dare to confront fate, even when victory is uncertain and the path ahead remains unknown. At its heart lies a simple yet powerful conviction: heroism is not defined solely by triumph, but by the willingness to stand against overwhelming circumstances without surrendering one’s dignity, conscience, or hope. Through poetic reflections on solitude, struggle, resilience, freedom, and the human spirit, this work portrays the act of drawing one’s sword against destiny as a symbol of existential courage rather than violence. The poem celebrates not only those who overcome adversity, but also those who continue forward despite failure, uncertainty, and the absence of recognition. Beyond its heroic imagery, the work embraces a deeper philosophy: true strength is not merely the power to resist, but also the capacity to protect, to remain compassionate, and to preserve warmth in a world that can often be unforgiving. Created within the imaginative framework of the White Rainbow Era, this literary work reflects the principle of Strength-Grounded Warmth—a vision of kindness supported by courage, boundaries, responsibility, and inner conviction. Ultimately, DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY offers a tribute to every ordinary person who has ever faced an extraordinary struggle. Its central message is timeless: To dare to challenge destiny is already an act of heroism. Victory may belong to circumstance, but courage belongs to the one who dares.
items.title: ⚔️ English Title DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY

items.summary: Code and data to reproduce all analyses and the figure in Sellers et al. (2026) “Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama’s anchoveta fishery and its exports”. Includes Python scripts for the bay-wide composite upwelling index, the observer set records, the unified 1956 to 2025 landings series, the main figure, and every statistic reported in the paper and its Supporting Information. Data include weekly sonde casts from the three deep central stations of the Bay of Panama, reef temperature loggers in the Gulf of Panama running since 1995, the Copernicus Marine Service biogeochemical reanalysis of net primary production (1994 to 2026), anchoveta and thread herring landings spliced from the digitised national stock assessment (1956 to 2014) and the ARAP landings register (2015 to 2025), 3,077 onboard observer purse-seine set records (2017 to 2025), 645 dockside proximate assays of landed anchoveta (2016 to 2025), and fish oil and fishmeal export tabulations from INEC customs statistics (1997 to 2025). Version 2.0 accompanies the revised manuscript and corrects three errors in version 1.0 (the units of the 1956 to 2005 landings, a wrongly masked grid cell in the production analysis, and a duplicated logger record), as listed in README.md. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 and code under the MIT Licence.
items.title: Code and data for: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports

items.summary: Added inverse_predict(model, result, reading, bracket, reading_sigma=0.0, theta=None, cov=None, n_scan=1001, max_slope_change=0.1) : reads a calibration curve backwards. It finds the setting x0 at which the model predicts a new reading inside the given bracket (a scan of n_scan points for sign changes, then bisection) and its error bar by first-order propagation through the implicit function, u(x0)^2 = (u(y0)^2 + a^T C a) / s^2 (JCGM 100:2008, section 5.2), split into the part from the reading and the part from the calibration. Several readings give the full covariance (they share the calibration). For a straight line it is the propagation-of-error formula of the NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 2.3.6.7.3 (https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section3/mpc3673.htm). Refuses a reading the model does not reach in the bracket or reaches more than once, a model that is flat at the solution, and a solution where the slope changes by more than max_slope_change (10 %) within one error bar, where a first-order error bar is not reliable. runs_test(residuals, order=None) : the runs test of A. Wald and J. Wolfowitz, Ann. Math. Statist. 11, 147-162 (1940), doi:10.1214/aoms/1177731909, on the signs of the residuals ordered by the setting. Finds a systematic misfit (a bend, a drift) that chi-squared misses when the reading errors are overstated. Exact tail probabilities of the number of runs, p_value (too few runs) and p_value_high (too many), with the mean and standard deviation of the number of runs. Tutorials examples/tutorial_calibration_curve.py and examples/tutorial_decay_on_background.py (see Tutorials below). README examples 13 ( inverse_predict ) and 14 ( runs_test ), and a Tutorials section, each with output obtained by running it. Fixed Model.numeric_jacobian (and so information , design , fit and propagate ) refused a valid model at a valid parameter as "non-finite". A parameter whose relative step does not change the predictions by 1e-8 of their largest value falls back to the 0.1.0 step 1e-6 * max(|theta|, 1e-3) , which is 1e-9 for a parameter below 1e-3: for a time constant of 1e-9 s it is the parameter itself. A decay of amplitude 10 on a background of 1000 (any amplitude below about 1/73 of the background), tau = 1e-9 s, samples from t = 0: tau - h = 0 , the model divided 0 by 0, and before the fix information , design and fit from that guess raised "the forward function returned non-finite predictions". After: the step is divided by 10 until the model is finite (at most 8 times) and then checked as before; the planned error bar on tau (reading error 1) is 1.4189183e-10 s, the exact value from the analytic slopes to 6e-9 relative, and the fit equals the fit with exact slopes to 1e-4 of an error bar. Steps that already gave finite predictions are used as before, so every result 0.3.0 could compute is unchanged (test test_fallback_step_that_reaches_zero_is_cut , which fails on 0.3.0, and test_fallback_cut_does_not_touch_working_steps ). Changed Clearer refusals: Model.numeric_jacobian (which Model.jacobian uses when the model has no jac ) refuses a rel_step that is not a finite positive number (0.3.0 raised UnboundLocalError for 0 or a negative step); coverage_exact refuses an n that is not a whole number (0.3.0 returned 0.9 for coverage_exact(29.9, 0.1) , the answer for n = 29). Packaging (from the unreleased notes after 0.3.0): the license is given as the SPDX expression license = "Apache-2.0" with license-files = ["LICENSE"] ; the old license table and license classifier are gone. Building no longer prints setuptools' deprecation warnings (their support ends on 2027-02-18). Building from source needs setuptools 77 or newer; installing the package is unchanged. README: the new functions, refusals, tests, the 0.4.0 correction, limits and sources; a word guide entry for residuals and runs and one for inverse prediction. The printed output of README examples 1
items.title: labplan: exact measurement planning, calibration and audit trails for any lab model

items.summary: Although room impulse responses (RIRs) encode source-distance cues, conventional monaural source separation focuses on recovering audio content without estimating source-specific RIRs, losing the associated spatial information. To address this limitation, we propose Distance-Aware Monaural Source Separation using Multi-RIR Estimation (DAMSEP), the first end-to-end framework that is jointly trained for source separation and multi-source RIR estimation from a single-microphone mixture. DAMSEP integrates a separation backbone with shared dereverberation and RIR estimation modules to jointly recover clean sources and source-specific complex convolutive transfer functions under source estimation and reverberant reconstruction objectives, enabling relative near/far ordering through the direct-to-reverberant ratios of the corresponding RIRs. For comprehensive evaluation, we introduce HETMIXR, which spans heterogeneous source content and diverse simulated room conditions with source-specific RIRs and geometric distance annotations. Experiments on HETMIXR demonstrate superior performance in source separation, RIR estimation, and distance ordering. Ablation studies reveal the complementary benefits of source supervision and reverberant reconstruction, while additional evaluations show generalization to single-speaker inputs and mixtures generated using measured RIRs from an unseen room. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Wenanzhi/DAMSEP.
items.title: DAMSEP: Distance-Aware Monaural Source Separation using Multi-RIR Estimation

items.summary: Code, archived production results and figure scripts that reproduce the numbers and figures of two companion papers on a small flat universe, a cubic three-torus that begins at a Casimir turning point: A. Zhang, Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins (2026), a Letter; A. Zhang, A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe (2026). The companion technical report, A. Zhang, Casimir Cosmology: Derivations and Numerical Validation, version 1.0 (2026), is deposited as a separate record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23434140; a copy is included in docs/technical_report/. Contents. Four chains of result directories: casimir/ (Standard Model Casimir weight, gauge and Higgs zero-mode energy, shape Hessian), higgs/ (finite-volume criterion for the Higgs zero mode: Standard Model couplings at the turning-point scale, one-loop finite-volume matching, two-dimensional zero-mode model with cross terms, hazard integral, critical top-quark masses and error budget, real-time ξ_H condition, robustness, universality, two-branch analysis), shape/ (emptiness gate, real-moment theorem, shape fossil, nonlinear survival, Moyal and Wheeler–DeWitt checks, primordial spectra) and cmb/ (temperature and polarization covariance of a three-torus, Fisher information and exact Kullback–Leibler divergences, fossil ensemble, joint inflaton–shape state). Every result directory has a quick and a full mode and compares fresh output with the archived production values under stated tolerances; python run_all.py --quick reproduces the quick checks and all figures. validation/ archives the independent reimplementations of the main results, with their specifications, code and outputs, and compares them with the main calculation. numbers/ is the single source of the numbers quoted in the papers and in the report. cmb/02_ensemble/data/ contains the ℓ ≤ 80 CAMB transfer table. Verification. On a fresh copy of this release (Python 3.12, Windows 11), python run_all.py --quick passes in all 25 verification runs (241 of 242 checks passed, 1 optional check skipped: the compiled SMDR refit), and the 51 shared numbers of the papers and the report (numbers/) agree with the archived outputs. Details and known limitations are given in RELEASE_NOTES.md. Integrity. MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS.txt list the size and SHA-256 of every file; python tools/sha256sums.py check verifies a copy. This record archives release v1.0.0 of https://github.com/Ailun-Zhang/casimir-cosmology. Licenses. Code: MIT. Data and text: CC BY 4.0. The SMDR 1.3 tarball (shipped unmodified) and the four files derived from or linked against it: GPL-2.0-or-later (see README.md, section License).
items.title: Code and data for: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe

items.summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) have made substantial progress in audio understanding. However, in high-throughput applications requiring frequent selection, judgment, and scoring, autoregressive text generation introduces additional computational overhead and response latency. To address this limitation, we introduce Qwen-Audio-Jev by augmenting Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next with a dedicated Jev decision head. The model unifies selection, binary judgment, and scoring through three decision primitives: CHOICE, NOUL, and SCORE. Given audio, a natural-language question, and an explicit answer specification, it directly produces a task-conditioned probability distribution or a numerical score through typed decision readouts. Evaluation across 18 labeled configurations covers all three primitives: for CHOICE, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves accuracies of 78.70% on MMAU-mini and 84.06% on MMSU; for NOUL, it achieves an equal error rate of 6.50% on the VoxCeleb1-O speaker verification benchmark; and for SCORE, the model achieves a normalized mean absolute error of 0.1062 on NISQA overall quality assessment, with Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.8210 and 0.8074, respectively. Compared with the original Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves an approximately 20x inference speedup. It demonstrates its potential for efficient, high-throughput audio decision-making in applications such as large-scale audio screening, speaker verification, and automated quality assessment.
items.title: Qwen-Audio-Jev: A Unified Interface for Audio Decisions

items.summary: The rapid expansion of the gig economy, facilitated by digital talent platforms, has fundamentally reconfigured the nature of work, employment relationships, and organizational structures. This paradigm shift from stable, long-term employment to a fluid workforce of contractors, freelancers, and project-based talent presents profound challenges to conventional leadership theories and practices. Traditional models, predicated on hierarchical authority, stable organizational boundaries, and enduring psychological contracts, are proving increasingly inadequate for orchestrating a workforce characterized by autonomy, transience, and distributed networks. This paper conducts a critical review of existing leadership literature—including transformational, adaptive, and emerging platform leadership theories—assessing their applicability and limitations in the gig context. Synthesizing insights from organizational behavior, strategic management, and technology studies, we propose a novel integrated framework: the Fluid Leadership Ecosystem (FLE) Model. The FLE model conceptualizes leadership not as a function of individual authority but as the cultivation of a dynamic ecosystem across three core dimensions: Relational Architecture, Algorithmic Stewardship, and Capability Cultivation. We argue that effective leadership in this new era requires designing trust-enabling infrastructures, ensuring human-centric governance of management algorithms, and fostering portable skill development for a transient workforce. This paper introduces novel theoretical perspectives, including temporal leadership dynamics, polycontextual leadership challenges, and the concept of reverse leadership flows from workers to platforms. By presenting a comprehensive model supported by data visualizations and identifying avenues for empirical validation, this research offers a forward-looking agenda for both scholars and practitioners navigating the complexities of leadership in the 21st-century workforce.
items.title: The Gig Economy and Talent Platforms: New Models of Leadership for Managing a Fluid Workforce

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
items.title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

items.summary: Speech anonymization is evaluated with automatic speaker verification attackers whose performance depends on the attribute distribution of both their training and evaluation data, which may bias privacy estimates for some speaker groups. To alleviate this issue, we introduce VoxAnon, a dataset built from VoxCeleb1 and 2 with training and evaluation splits balanced across gender, age, accent, and pitch. We extract and cross-check attributes using two complementary methods, balance trial lists per subgroup, and draw test/enrollment utterances from distinct video sources in order to limit linguistic and session bias. Comparing VoxAnon with unbalanced training and test data across four attackers and three anonymizers, we show that attribute imbalance changes which subgroups appear hardest to re-identify, in directions that depend on the attribute. In the balanced setting, residual disparities persist, mostly tied to accent and pitch, and depend on the anonymizer/attacker pair. Code and trial lists are publicly available.
items.title: VoxAnon: A balanced dataset for a fair evaluation of speech anonymization
